title: Nanosight LM10 Cleaning Protocol
author: Joshua A Welsh
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfetjjen
materials: Open up the most recent version of the NanoSight software (3.4 as of January 2020)
Turn the camera on inside the NTA software by clicking "Start camera"
Current temperature: Measure using thermometer on table
At the end of the 3 captures, allow the software to automatically analyze the data
If you need to measure another sample:
Turn the camera on inside the NTA software by clicking "Start camera"
To adjust settings, press: SOP - 1. Standard Measurement 2. Number of Captures: 3 3. Capture Duration(s): 30 4. Current temperature: Measure using thermometer on table

steps.title: System Power-Up
steps.instruction: Initialize the hardware and computer systems.

substeps.instruction: Turn on the black power strip.
Turn on the computer on the shelf and login using the password written above the screen.
Turn on the Nanosight microscope (confirm the camera fan turns on).

steps.title: Inspect and Clean Optical Components
steps.instruction: Prepare the LM10 module by removing the cover and cleaning the optics if necessary.

substeps.instruction: Remove the storage lens paper from between the stainless steel cover and the optical flat of the LM10 module.
Inspect the optical flat and the steel cover window for smudges or particles.
Clean the outside of the window using a can of compressed air to remove dust and lint.

Clean the inside of the window: pour a small amount of 1% MICRO 90 into the cap of a 50 mL conical, dip a folded piece of lens paper into it, and gently clean the surface. Repeat this process using a new piece of lens paper dipped in DPBS, then dry with lens paper.

Clean the optical flat: pour 1% MICRO 90 into the cap of a 50 mL conical, dip a folded piece of lens paper into it, and wipe the optical flat (focusing on the translucent rectangle). Press firmly perpendicularly and parallel to the edge; do not wipe in circles.

steps.title: Reassemble Module
steps.instruction: Secure the steel cover back onto the module.

substeps.instruction: Quickly place the steel cover back onto the module.
Screw it in, tightening the screws in a diagonal pattern, ensuring not to over-tighten.

steps.title: Flush LM10 Module with DPBS
steps.instruction: Clear the module of contaminants using DPBS.

substeps.instruction: Load 10 mL of DPBS into a 12 mL syringe.
Insert the syringe into the white plastic entry port (the only port on its side) and slowly inject DPBS while holding the module vertically to avoid bubbles on the viewing window.
Once liquid fills the fluid exit port, flip the module so the syringe is standing straight up and slowly press the plunger until all DPBS passes into a waste container.
If bubbles form, push them all the way through; do not reverse the syringe.
Return the module to its vertical position and slowly draw out remaining DPBS from the viewing window.
Discard the used DPBS in a waste container.
Draw up another 6 mL of DPBS. If bubbles were present in the initial flush, push the entire volume through and add another 6 mL.
Flush the NanoSight with ~5 mL of DPBS, leaving less than 1 mL in the syringe.

steps.title: Microscope Setup and Alignment
steps.instruction: Position the module and configure the software settings.

substeps.instruction: Slide the LM10 module into the grooved slot on the microscope table.
Ensure the 20X lens is in use.

Apply the following settings for the 405 nm LM10 module: Capture (Screen Gain: 1, Camera Level: 14), Process (Screen Gain: 1, Detection Threshold: 4), Advanced (Uncheck all 'AUTO' boxes, Min Track Length: 8).
Plug the power source into the side of the LM10 module.
Turn on the laser by flipping the silver switch on the right side of the LM10 module.

steps.title: Calibrate Viewing Window
steps.instruction: Align the microscope to the correct analysis area.

substeps.instruction: Use focusing knobs/stage mover to locate the viewing window.
Center the 'thumb-print' (a large purple oval) in the microscope window.
Move the screen to the right until a large vertical line appears. Position the viewing frame immediately to the right of this line (as close as possible without the line being in the window).
If the line is not vertical, slightly rotate the camera module on top of the microscope.

steps.title: Verify Module Cleanliness
steps.instruction: Ensure the system is free of particles before sample loading.

substeps.instruction: Check for remaining particles from previous samples.
If particles are present: turn off the laser, disconnect power, get a new aliquot of PBS and a new syringe, and repeat the flushing process.

If large fluorescent smudges or significant white background noise are present: turn off the laser, disconnect power, clean the optical flat and viewing window, and flush the module (repeating steps 6-15).
If clear, turn off the laser and slowly pull the remaining PBS out with the syringe.

steps.title: Sample Preparation and Loading
steps.instruction: Prepare and introduce the sample into the module.

substeps.instruction: Dilute samples as needed in a 2 mL low protein-binding Eppendorf tube and vortex thoroughly.
Draw the sample into a 1 mL syringe, pulling the plunger down to remove bubbles.
Load the sample into the LM10 module through the fluid entry port.
Turn on the laser.

steps.title: Sample Analysis and Recording
steps.instruction: Capture data and manage sample flow.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the sample is in the correct viewing window, properly focused, and at the correct concentration (too dilute if <20 particles; too concentrated if significant background noise or particles overlap).
Press 'Create and run script,' enter sample name and dilution, and click 'OK'.
When the fan turns off, the instrument is recording; ensure the table is not bumped or vibrated.
After each 30-second capture, press 'OK' and carefully press the plunger until particles on the screen move.
Turn off the laser as soon as data analysis begins.
Click 'Export' once data analysis is complete.

steps.title: Post-Analysis Flush
steps.instruction: Clean the module after sample recording.

substeps.instruction: Flush the device with at least 2x12 mL syringes of DPBS.
Check the viewing frame to ensure it is particle-free and without smudges.
If particles remain, the module must be opened and cleaned as described in the initial cleaning steps.

steps.title: Final System Shutdown and Cleaning
steps.instruction: Perform deep cleaning and power down the system.

substeps.instruction: Open the module and wipe the optical flat with 1% MICRO 90.
Wipe the optical flat with a piece of lens paper gently wetted with pure water, then dry with a new piece of dry lens paper.

Wipe all components that contacted DPBS (including sides, corners, and edges) with a Kimwipe or lens paper wetted with pure water, then dry with compressed air. Do not pour or pipette water directly onto the module.
Place a piece of folded, dry lens paper between the optical flat and steel cover plate.
Turn off all power sources.

steps.title: Data Transfer
steps.instruction: Export recorded data to a flash drive.

substeps.instruction: Navigate to: This PC -> J'D (H:) -> Nanosight files -> Nanovideos -> Date of recording.
